caption: A water balloon is dropped from a second-floor balcony, and it falls straight down and bursts on the pavement.

sa.check: A water balloon is dropped from a second-floor balcony.
The balcony and the pavement below are both visible.
The release comes first, then the fall, then the burst.

pc.expect: The balloon starts to fall at the release, drops along a line below the balcony, and falls quicker the further it goes.
pc.fail: The balloon drifts sideways out from under the balcony; or it slows as it falls; or it hangs in the air below the balcony.

pc.expect: It bursts where it meets the pavement and not before; the water spreads out on the ground and stays there.
pc.fail: The balloon bursts in mid-air before touching the pavement; or it hits the pavement and bounces away still whole; or the water lands and leaves the pavement dry.

pc.expect: One balloon goes down and the water on the ground is the water it carried.
pc.fail: A second balloon appears during the fall; or the balloon vanishes before reaching the pavement; or a wet patch spreads on the ground before the balloon lands.

pc.expect: The balloon bulges and wobbles as a bag of liquid on the way down and its skin tears open on impact.
pc.fail: The balloon stays a rigid ball through the fall and the impact; or it squashes and springs back whole off the pavement; or it shrinks slowly as if leaking air instead of bursting.

pc.expect: The balloon, the balcony and the pavement stay solid.
pc.fail: The balloon passes through the pavement; or it passes through the balcony rail on the way down; or it merges into the wall of the building.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The balloon's colour, the balcony and the pavement stay the same.
pc.fail: The balloon changes colour during the fall; or the balcony railing changes pattern between frames; or the pavement's paving changes layout.
